Planning and coordinating cultural arts infrastructure development activities including RMK.
Coordinating requirements related to staging, audiovisual, and production.
Ensuring that all production, staging, and audio-visual requirements operate smoothly in accordance with production needs.

Responsible for general management, financial management, and resource management. It is now been expanded to include public relations management, information systems, and cultural arts infrastructure development.

Responsible for financial management aspects, including planning, preparation of budget estimates, allocation of funds, procurement, accounts and payments, expenditure control, virement, record-keeping, and reconciliation.
Carrying out duties encompassing public relations activities, information systems, and cultural arts infrastructure development.

Conducting research on classification applications, certifying classification codes, and removing or cancelling dockets and evaluation circulars.
Drafting orders and subsidiary customs legislation, and providing valuation advisory services and open market price studies.
Leading raids, investigations, prosecutions, roadblocks, and patrols.
Processing licence applications, preparing master licensing records, and conducting premise inspections for certification.
Processing and endorsing duty payments, including domestic trade duties and excise duties under the Blanket System.
Preparing account inspection reports, operational and management task audits, and offering compounds.
Preparing development expenditure estimates, analysing training requirements, and providing advisory services on trade and industrial facilitation.

Maintain accurate tax records, documentation, and reports in line with professional standards.

Planning, managing, and conducting courses and training for Civil Defence officers of all grades; team instructors for all divisions, including units and Civil Defence cadets to be established; and special courses for Civil Defence Officers, and courses for other organisations, such as Youth Associations, the Red Crescent, Red Crescent Committees, Rukun Tetangga, firms, government departments, and statutory bodies.

Studying and developing required training programmes.

Studying equipment and operational requirements.
Conducting and monitors development and research activities to meet the knowledge requirements of officers within the service scheme.
Preparing the Annual Work Target (Sasaran Kerja Tahunan, SKT) and the Annual Performance Appraisal Report (Laporan Nilaian Prestasi Tahunan, LNPT) for staff under supervision.
Performing duties during emergencies and disasters, as directed.
Implementing, reviewing, and coordinating national and international labour policies, workforce management, labour research, as well as job standards and classifications.

Conducting statutory inspections, farm and night inspections, complaint investigations, investigation reports, and follow-up actions.

Conducting mentions and hearings for claims cases, maintaining registers, and undertaking follow-up actions on court orders.
Undertaking prosecution/compound actions against violations of labour laws and regulations.

Managing the registration, modification, dissolution, and enforcement of trade unions.
Conducting investigations, arbitration, preparation of investigation papers, affidavits, and proposals for amendments to trade union laws.
Implementing enforcement, investigation, prosecution, conciliation, and arbitration activities under labour, industrial relations, trade union legislation, and the PSMB Act 2001.

Implementing security controls under the Official Secrets Act 1972 and the Kawasan Larangan/Tempat Larangan 1959; plans, coordinates, executes, advises, monitors, and enforces the protection of premises, documents, and personal security.

Formulating and coordinating the Security Protection Policy and official information, investigating security breaches, providing technical advice, assessing vulnerabilities, and recommending corrective actions.
Developing personnel security and screening policies, investigating violations, trains and educates public servants, and administering examinations for Officers, Assistants, and Security Guards.

Coordinating security policies and equipment, managing security passes and departmental identity cards, authority cards, and appointment cards, providing technical advice on the selection of security companies, managing restricted areas and critical targets, and investigates physical security breaches.

Formulating and implementing policies, providing training and advisory services, planning Tim Naziran programmes, investigating security violations, and recommending actions.

Leading, heading, planning, controlling, supervising, coordinating, analysing, motivating, and managing the divisional/prison institution organisation in achieving the department’s vision, mission, and objectives.
Leading maximum-security prison institutions.
Leading the divisional/prison institution organisation and synthesising multiple functional areas to achieve departmental excellence efficiently and professionally.
Leading the divisional/prison institution organisation and conducting analysis of programmes implemented within prison management.
Leading, coordinating, and monitoring all functions at the divisional organisation and prison institution levels.
Leading and spearheading reforms and innovations at the divisional organisation and prison institution levels.
Planing and formulating policies for divisional organisations and institutions.
Planning and controlling financial management and procurement to achieve effective management objectives.
Responsible for planning, coordinating, formulating, and reviewing relevant laws and regulations.
Coordinating the effectiveness and improvement of security management and existing rehabilitation programmes being implemented in prison institutions.
Enforcing law and order under federal law within the Malaysian Maritime Zone.
Formulating navigational policies and implementing security policies for the Malaysian Maritime Zone.
Planning logistics management and operational planning.

Carrying out maritime search and rescue duties, aerial and coastal surveillance, maritime pollution control and prevention, prevention and blocking of swarming, as well as prevention and blocking of illicit narcotic drug trafficking.
Ensuring the smoothness and effectiveness of assistance in any criminal matter at the request of a foreign country as provided under the Mutual Assistance in Criminal Matters Act 2002 (Act 621).
Ensuring rig services and support to relevant agencies are provided efficiently and effectively.
Collecting and evaluating security intelligence information and proposing enhancements to operational effectiveness.
Ensuring the efficiency and effectiveness of maritime and aerial patrols and operations conducted within the Malaysian Maritime Zone.
Implementing and enhancing the quality of personnel training, operational training, and joint training within the country’s maritime areas.
Establishing close relations with other departments/ agencies in relation to law enforcement within the Malaysian Maritime Zone.
Conducting open investigations, supervises investigation papers, arrests, detentions, prosecutions, and prepares case reports.
Responsible as the Investigation Officer for investigation papers, intelligence, surveillance, and undercover projects.
Collecting and analysing information on corruption, misappropriation, and abuse of power, and recruits, trains, and supervises information sources.
Planning, designing, coordinating, and evaluating community education programmes, public awareness, publications, exhibitions, and studies on the effectiveness of corruption prevention.

Preparing proposal papers on recommendations to conduct inspections of the practices, systems, and procedures of government departments, and provides advisory services and monitoring of the implementation of recommendations.
Conducting prosecutions in Court, managing applications for subpoenas, reviewing Court decisions, and preparing trial case reports.
Preparing policy papers, strategic planning documents, directives, guidelines, and regulations, and conducting social research and studies on the level of corruption.
Managing and coordinates training programmes, forensic courses, training research, international programmes, and the organisation of conventions.
Managing physical security, documents, witnesses, detention facilities, authority cards, security passes, and escorts.
Managing procurement, budgets, contracts, reports, unit administration, and carrying out other duties as directed by senior officers.

Analysing, planning, and formulating policies for open investigations, supervising investigations of corruption and abuse of power in the private sector and privatised government agencies, and preparing reports and statistics for the Forensic Accounting Unit.
Providing assistance, accounting services, and tracing assets suspected to be proceeds of corruption, and coordinating networking with domestic and foreign agencies.

Supervising and managing intelligence, surveillance, projects, and the collection of information related to corruption, misappropriation, and abuse of power, and recruits, trains, and supervises potential information sources contributing corruption-related information.
Planning, designing, coordinating, and evaluating community education programmes, public awareness, publications, exhibitions, and studies on the effectiveness of corruption prevention programmes.

Preparing proposal papers and conducting inspections of practices, systems, and procedures of government departments, reviewing intelligence reports, investigations, BPA, audits, and providing advisory services and monitors the implementation of proposal.
Conducting prosecutions in Court, reviewing decisions of the Lower Courts, providing expert opinions, and managing the administration of court trial files.

Planning and organising anti-corruption courses, training programmes, basic/promotion courses, training at government centres, distance learning/local university programmes, and international conventions.
Performing scheduled and assigned duties as directed by senior officers, managing officer assignments, assisting the Unit Head/Branch Head, and serving in Parliament.

Analysing, planning, and formulating policies for open investigations involving the economic interests and revenue of the nation, conducting investigations into sensitive corruption cases, and reviewing and prepares investigation reports.

Designing and publishing anti-corruption publications and exhibition materials for community education programmes.

Planning, implementing, supervising, coordinating, and evaluating branch activities; conducting inspections of practices, systems, and procedures of public bodies, providing advisory services and monitoring, and preparing inputs for intelligence and investigation activities.
Analysing international corruption issues and studies for research and planning purposes.
Planning, developing modules, and leading training programmes, including Forensic Accounting, Forensic Construction, and Forensic Computer courses.
Managing physical security, documents, personnel, armaments, detention facilities, escorts, witness protection, authority cards, security passes, and access to BPR offices.

Supervising information management and disciplinary matters, ensuring complaints, Corruption Reporting Information System (C-RIS), Toll-Free Line (TAP), and daily reports from the Information Receiving Unit (UMM) are handled accurately, and monitoring disciplinary cases involving officers and staff.

Performing scheduled and assigned duties as directed by senior officers, managing officer assignments in branches/units, and assisting the Unit Head and Branch Head in overseeing divisional activities.

Planning, monitoring, and supervising activities of the Special Intelligence Branch, Risk Branch, Surveillance Branch, Project Implementation Branch, Zone Control Branch, Technical Services Branch, and Intelligence Administration Branch, including the collection of information on corruption, misappropriation, and abuse of power.
Planning, designing, and coordinating public awareness, education, and community relations programmes.

Planning, supervising, and evaluating branch activities, conducting inspections of practices, systems, and procedures of government departments, providing advisory services, and preparing periodic reports and inputs for intelligence and investigation activities.

Supervising and prepares strategic planning papers, drafts of the Director General’s Standing Orders, directives and guidelines, updating legal provisions, and conducting social research and studies on the level of corruption.
Planning and supervising courses, seminars, workshops, and international conventions.
Performing scheduled duties, managing officer assignments, and assisting the Unit Head/Branch Head in overseeing divisional activities.
Serving in Parliament and executing directives from senior authorities.

Planning, supervising, reviewing, and discussing all investigations under the APR 1997 and AMLATFA 2001, including asset forfeiture, expert reports, wiretaps, account applications, and suspect extraditions.
Planning, supervising, and controlling intelligence, surveillance, projects, information acquisition, and management of sources.

Planning, coordinating, and monitoring public awareness, education, community relations programmes, anti-corruption publications and exhibitions, and evaluating the effectiveness of corruption prevention programmes.
Supervising and evaluates inspections of practices, systems, and procedures of public/private bodies and organisations, and providing advisory services.
Preparing policy papers, strategic planning documents, new directives and guidelines, monitoring the implementation of meetings, Parliamentary matters, and corruption-related surveys.
Managing academy administration, analysing training needs, planning annual training programmes, and coordinating officer/staff participation in domestic and international training.
Liaising with international anti-corruption and enforcement agencies for the identification of witnesses, suspects, and overseas assets, as well as extradition processes.

Executing directives from senior officers, manages officer assignments, assists the Unit Head/Branch Head, and serves in Parliament.

Collect soil samples from field sites and conduct field inspections as required.

Conduct field inspections to monitor slope stability and identify potential hazards.

Monitor inventory levels, assist in ordering supplies, and support equipment calibration and maintenance.

Assisting in chemical analysis of metals, alloys, clays, limestone, silicate sand, ceramics, ores, groundwater, coal, and exploration samples such as sediments, soils, and others; and conducting physical testing of industrial mineral samples such as clay, sand, and ceramic materials.
Maintaining laboratory cleanliness, safety, analytical procedures, and research and development (R&D) of nuclear or related technologies.
Assisting in the implementation of quality management systems ISO/IEC 17025, MS ISO 9000, and OHSAS 18001 occupational safety standards.
Managing documents, Permits To Work, quarantines, environmental control, hazardous cargo, and monitors port operations.
